pages.title: ZEPHYR
pages.meta: BSc thesis, graded 9.5 out of 10. Being extended into a paper for ICRA 2027
body: A navigation framework for drones with three modes. Gaussian and inverse power potential fields handle open flight, a policy trained with PPO handles escaping from traps, and an arbiter decides which mode is active.
The main finding was about the arbiter. Replacing a reactive Schmitt trigger with a predictive selector raised the success rate from 0.514 to 0.963, with the same controllers underneath.
I also compared it with DWA on safety. The field planner kept a safe distance from obstacles in 98.4% of steps, and DWA in 34.7%.

pages.title: DAEDALUS
body: A pipeline that turns a poem into an SVG drawing. Word embeddings are passed through compositional pattern producing networks (CPPNs) evolved with NEAT, so the meaning of the text decides the structure of the image.
It does not use any existing artworks or image datasets, which avoids questions about provenance and consent.
On longer texts the graph layout still produces tangled edges. This limitation is documented in the paper.

pages.title: ATLAS
pages.meta: Pass ranking with geometry. Manuscript prepared for npj Artificial Intelligence, AI in Sports
body: A pass ranking framework that uses four geometric penalties (triangle, vector, radius and direction) and no learned model.
I evaluated it on StatsBomb event data from Euro 2020 and Euro 2024 with H@3 and P@3, a sensitivity analysis and z tests for two proportions.
The direction penalty contributed the most to the result.

pages.title: Damage recovery using Transformers
body: A locomotion controller with a transformer inside, built in MuJoCo Gymnasium and optimised with evolutionary algorithms. It learns to keep walking after part of its body is damaged.
With damage it reached higher average returns than without damage, and attention made it tolerant to faults without retraining.

pages.title: GraphRAG
pages.meta: Python, Llama 3.2, OWL, OWLAPY, Manchester syntax
body: A system that translates travel questions in natural language into formal ontology queries, using Llama 3.2 prompted with a few examples.

When a query has no results, a reasoner removes constraints one at a time with a recursive algorithm based on regular expressions. It retrieved the right hotels in 95% of queries with three to five constraints.

pages.title: Curriculum learning
body: An adaptive curriculum for a Point Maze environment with three difficulty levels, trained with TQC, hindsight experience replay and reward shaping that decreases over time.
Statistical tests over several seeds showed that the curricula performed the same.

pages.title: Strategic Noisy SGD
pages.meta: PyTorch, LSTM. London temperatures from 1979 to 2023
body: A version of stochastic gradient descent that adds noise which keeps the sign of the gradient and decreases over time. I tested it on a two layer LSTM that forecasts daily temperature.
The study includes comparisons with baselines, Bayesian hyperparameter optimisation, and an analysis of errors and residuals.

pages.title: Analogue Intelligence website
pages.meta: The website of the research lab
body: A 3D building in Three.js that you can walk through, with six rooms, custom shaders, characters and achievements. It has no build step and uses plain ES modules.

pages.title: My Own World
pages.meta: The site you are using now
body: A portrait made from two planes with depth maps, rendered at low resolution. Her voice is generated in the browser and her mouth moves with it.
You can read my CV as a plain page or explore the inside of my mind, a 3D landscape with books about my work.

pages.title: How I work
body: I run ablations before I decide what a result means. Several of my results changed after I tested the parts one at a time.
I report the metrics that show weaknesses as well as strengths. For example, a success rate of 0.999 is not enough if the system is unsafe in most steps.
I write the limitations early, because they often point to the next project.
